910.name: Illyrian & Roman Doclea
910.description: The Illyrian tribes of the Montenegrin coast and hinterland were gradually incorporated into the Roman Empire. The city of Doclea (near modern Podgorica) became a significant Roman municipium and later gave its name to the medieval state.

sub_clusters.name: Illyrian Tribes & Greek Coastal Contacts
sub_clusters.description: The Ardiaei and Labeates Illyrian tribes dominating the region, Greek colonies on the coast, and Queen Teuta's conflicts with Rome leading to the Illyrian Wars.

sub_clusters.name: Roman Doclea & Province of Prevalis
sub_clusters.description: Roman conquest and incorporation into Illyricum, the founding of Doclea as a municipium, Emperor Diocletian's reorganisation creating the province of Prevalis, and early Christian communities.
key_events: Roman defeat of Illyrian King Gentius (168 BCE)
Diocletian creates the province of Prevalis (c. 297 CE)

920.name: Principality of Duklja & Zeta
920.description: South Slavic settlement created the principality of Duklja (Doclea), which evolved into the kingdom of Zeta. Under the Vojislavljević dynasty, Montenegro emerged as a distinct political entity between Byzantine, Serbian, and Venetian spheres.

sub_clusters.name: Slavic Settlement & Rise of Duklja
sub_clusters.description: Arrival of South Slavs, the formation of Duklja as a principality under Byzantine suzerainty, and growing autonomy under local dynasties.

sub_clusters.name: Kingdom of Duklja under the Vojislavljević
sub_clusters.description: Stefan Vojislav's revolt against Byzantium, Mihailo's recognition as king by Pope Gregory VII (1077), and the golden age of Duklja before absorption into the Nemanjić Serbian state.
key_events: Pope Gregory VII recognises Mihailo as King of Duklja (1077)

920.name: Zeta under Nemanjić & Balšić Rule
920.description: Zeta became part of the Serbian Nemanjić realm, then re-emerged as a semi-independent entity under the Balšić and Crnojević noble families as Serbian central authority fragmented after the Battle of Kosovo.

sub_clusters.name: Zeta within Nemanjić Serbia
sub_clusters.description: Zeta as an appanage of the Nemanjić dynasty, including Stefan Dušan's empire, and the flourishing of Orthodox monasteries and coastal trade.

sub_clusters.name: Balšić Dynasty & Ottoman Advance
sub_clusters.description: The Balšić lords navigating between Ottoman, Venetian, and Serbian interests after the collapse of Dušan's empire and the catastrophe at Kosovo (1389).

930.name: Crnojević Dynasty & Ottoman Conquest
930.description: The Crnojević dynasty maintained Zeta's autonomy and established the famous Cetinje printing press (1494) before Ottoman conquest. Montenegro became the name of the mountainous core that resisted full Ottoman control.

sub_clusters.name: Crnojević Dynasty & Cetinje Press
sub_clusters.description: Ivan Crnojević's founding of Cetinje as capital, the establishment of one of the earliest South Slavic printing presses (Oktoih, 1494), and the gradual Ottoman encirclement.
key_events: Crnojević printing press at Cetinje publishes the Oktoih (1494)

sub_clusters.name: Ottoman Era & Tribal Resistance
sub_clusters.description: Nominal Ottoman suzerainty over the Montenegrin highlands, the role of the Cetinje bishopric as a focus of identity, and intermittent tribal revolts and Venetian alliances.

930.name: Petrović-Njegoš Prince-Bishops
930.description: The Petrović-Njegoš dynasty of vladike (prince-bishops) unified the Montenegrin tribes and waged continuous wars against the Ottomans. Petar II Petrović-Njegoš was both ruler and one of the greatest South Slavic poets.

sub_clusters.name: Vladika Danilo & Tribal Unification
sub_clusters.description: Danilo Petrović-Njegoš establishing hereditary theocratic rule, the alliance with Russia, and campaigns to expel Ottoman influence from the highlands.

sub_clusters.name: Petar II Njegoš & The Mountain Wreath
sub_clusters.description: The reign of Petar I (hero of the Napoleonic era) and Petar II Petrović-Njegoš, whose epic poem 'The Mountain Wreath' (1847) became a cornerstone of Montenegrin national identity.
key_events: Petar II Njegoš publishes 'The Mountain Wreath' (1847)

940.name: Secular Principality & International Recognition
940.description: Danilo II secularised Montenegro into a principality. Nikola I expanded territory through Ottoman wars, gained international recognition at the Congress of Berlin (1878), and elevated Montenegro to a kingdom in 1910.

sub_clusters.name: Danilo II & Secularisation
sub_clusters.description: Prince Danilo II's transformation of Montenegro from a theocracy to a secular principality, legal reforms, and his assassination in 1860.

sub_clusters.name: Congress of Berlin & International Recognition
sub_clusters.description: Prince Nikola I's Ottoman wars, expansion to the sea (Bar, Ulcinj), and Montenegro's recognition as a sovereign state at the Congress of Berlin (1878).
key_events: Congress of Berlin recognises Montenegrin independence (1878)

sub_clusters.name: Kingdom of Montenegro & Balkan Wars
sub_clusters.description: Nikola I's elevation to King (1910), modernisation efforts, the Balkan Wars (1912–13) doubling Montenegro's territory, and alliances leading to World War I.
key_events: Montenegro elevated to a kingdom under Nikola I (1910)

950.name: World Wars & Yugoslav Integration
950.description: Montenegro fought with the Allies in both World Wars. The controversial 1918 Podgorica Assembly deposed King Nikola and merged Montenegro into the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, later Yugoslavia.

sub_clusters.name: WWI & Podgorica Assembly
sub_clusters.description: Montenegro's participation in World War I, the Austrian occupation, and the 1918 Podgorica Assembly that controversially voted for unification with Serbia, abolishing the Montenegrin monarchy.
key_events: Podgorica Assembly votes for unification with Serbia (26 Nov 1918)

sub_clusters.name: WWII – Resistance & Partisan Struggle
sub_clusters.description: Italian occupation, the July 1941 uprising (one of the earliest anti-Axis revolts in Europe), rivalry between Chetniks and Partisans, and Tito's liberation of Montenegro.

950.name: SR Montenegro in Socialist Yugoslavia
950.description: Montenegro was a constituent republic of Tito's Yugoslavia. Despite its small size, it enjoyed significant influence; the 'Anti-Bureaucratic Revolution' of 1989 brought Milošević allies to power.

sub_clusters.name: Titoist Montenegro & Industrialisation
sub_clusters.description: Montenegro's transformation under socialist Yugoslavia: industrialisation, development of the Adriatic coast, and the building of Montenegrin cultural institutions.

sub_clusters.name: Anti-Bureaucratic Revolution & Yugoslav Collapse
sub_clusters.description: The 1989 Anti-Bureaucratic Revolution installing pro-Milošević leadership, Montenegro's role in the Yugoslav Wars, and the formation of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia with Serbia.

960.name: Path to Independence (2006)
960.description: Montenegro gradually distanced itself from Serbia under Milo Đukanović, adopted the euro unilaterally, and voted for independence in a closely watched 2006 referendum.

sub_clusters.name: Federal Republic & Đukanović's Western Turn
sub_clusters.description: Montenegro within the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Đukanović's break with Milošević during the NATO bombing (1999), and the loose State Union of Serbia and Montenegro (2003).

sub_clusters.name: Independence Referendum (2006)
sub_clusters.description: The EU-brokered referendum of 21 May 2006 where 55.5% voted for independence, meeting the 55% threshold, and Montenegro's rapid international recognition.
key_events: Montenegro independence referendum passes with 55.5% (21 May 2006)

960.name: Euro-Atlantic Integration
960.description: Independent Montenegro pursued NATO and EU membership. NATO accession came in 2017 despite Russian opposition and an alleged coup attempt, while EU accession negotiations continue.

sub_clusters.name: NATO Accession & Alleged Coup Attempt
sub_clusters.description: Montenegro's NATO Membership Action Plan, the 2016 alleged Russian-backed coup attempt on election day, and formal NATO accession on 5 June 2017.
key_events: Montenegro joins NATO as 29th member (5 June 2017)
Alleged Russian-backed coup attempt on election day (16 Oct 2016)

sub_clusters.name: EU Candidacy & Modern Politics
sub_clusters.description: Ongoing EU accession negotiations, the 2020 election ending Đukanović's DPS dominance, political fragmentation, and debates over national identity.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
